name: Conservatory Glasshouse
desc: The inside of a Victorian conservatory: a barrel vault of glass and iron telescopes toward a misted vanishing point, condensation blooms on the panes, diffuse light banks down through the fog in slow shafts, and dark palm fronds hang into the frame and stir; a green-misted verdigris glasshouse, a bright clean daylight house, a moonlit nocturne, an abstracted cyan blueprint of the vault, or a warm-grey ink wash.

energy.doc: how brightly the light banks down — shaft intensity, mote glow and overall luminance

scale.doc: vault depth and frond size — from a distant deep house to a close vault with big fronds filling the frame

density.doc: how many mullions, motes and hanging fronds fill the house

speed.doc: rate of the drift — mote fall, shaft sweep and condensation trickle

haze.doc: how much condensation and fog veils the glass and gives the shafts their body

sway.doc: how much the fronds stir and the light shafts drift on the air

hue.doc: primary glass/foliage hue shift off the default green

x.doc: horizontal position of the vanishing point the vault recedes toward

y.doc: height of the vanishing point — where the vault converges

style.doc: aesthetic: verdigris = green-misted iron Kew glasshouse; glasshouse = bright clean warm daylight; nocturne = cold moonlit blue glass, black plants; blueprint = abstracted cyan line drawing of the vault, no glass fill; ink = abstracted warm-grey sumi wash

seed.doc: regenerates the condensation mottling, mullions and frond placement

alpha.doc: layer opacity — sinks the whole conservatory back behind the performers
